A.definition: Having more than one possible meaning or interpretation
A.example: The instructions were ambiguous and confusing.

A.definition: Showing selfless concern for the well-being of others
A.example: Her altruistic nature led her to volunteer at the shelter.

A.definition: Make something bad or unsatisfactory better
A.example: The new policies helped ameliorate the economic situation.

B.definition: Kind, generous, and caring about others
B.example: The benevolent donor provided funds for the new library.

B.definition: Relating to the pleasant aspects of the countryside
B.example: They enjoyed the bucolic scenery during their drive.

B.definition: Concise and exact use of words in writing or speech
B.example: The speaker was praised for the brevity of his speech.

C.definition: A harsh, discordant mixture of sounds
C.example: The cacophony of the city traffic was overwhelming.
She was cognizant of the risks involved.

C.definition: Given to sudden and unaccountable changes of mood or behavior
C.example: The capricious weather ruined their outdoor plans.

D.definition: Having or showing care and conscientiousness in one's work or duties
D.example: She was a diligent student who always completed her assignments.

D.definition: Skill in performing tasks, especially with the hands
Hesitating or doubting; not to be relied upon
D.example: They were dubious about the project's success.

E.definition: Lasting for a very short time
E.example: The ephemeral beauty of cherry blossoms.

E.definition: Fluent or persuasive in speaking or writing
E.example: Her eloquent speech moved the audience.

E.definition: Difficult to interpret or understand; mysterious
E.example: His enigmatic smile left them wondering.

F.definition: Very attentive to accuracy and detail
F.example: He was fastidious about keeping his workspace organized.

F.definition: Happening by chance rather than intention
F.example: Their fortuitous meeting led to a lifelong friendship.

F.definition: Attempting to avoid notice or attention, typically because of guilt or a belief that discovery would lead to trouble; secretive
F.example: He cast a furtive glance over his shoulder.

G.example: Her gregarious nature made her the life of every party.

G.definition: Excessively talkative, especially on trivial matters
G.example: The garrulous passenger talked throughout the journey.

G.definition: Uncalled for; lacking good reason; unwarranted

H.definition: A person or thing that announces or signals the approach of another
H.example: The robin is often seen as a harbinger of spring.

H.definition: Leadership or dominance, especially by one country or social group over others
H.example: The company's hegemony in the tech industry.

H.definition: Exaggerated statements or claims not meant to be taken literally
H.example: The claim that the pizza was 'the best in the universe' was pure hyperbole.

I.definition: Too great or extreme to be expressed or described in words
I.example: The ineffable beauty of the sunset left them speechless.

I.definition: Proceeding in a gradual, subtle way, but with harmful effects
I.example: The insidious spread of misinformation on social media.

I.definition: In accordance with the highest standards; faultless

J.definition: Place close together or side by side
J.example: The artist chose to juxtapose the old and new buildings.
The jovial host made everyone feel welcome.

J.definition: Having, showing, or done with good judgment or sense
J.example: He made a judicious decision to wait.

K.definition: Relating to or resulting from motion
K.example: The kinetic energy of the rushing water.
The kaleidoscopic patterns of the aurora borealis.

K.definition: Having or showing eagerness or enthusiasm
K.example: She had a keen interest in astronomy.

L.definition: Emitting light not caused by heat
L.example: The luminescent jellyfish glowed in the dark waters.

L.definition: Affected by lethargy; sluggish and apathetic
L.example: The hot weather made everyone feel lethargic.
Her lucid explanation helped clarify the concept.

M.definition: Sweet or musical; pleasant to hear
M.example: Her mellifluous voice captivated the audience.

M.definition: Showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise
M.example: His meticulous research impressed his professors.

M.definition: Very generous or forgiving, especially toward a rival or less powerful person

N.example: The detective uncovered their nefarious plot.

N.definition: Just coming into existence and beginning to display signs of future potential

O.example: The complex language seemed to obfuscate the simple truth.

O.definition: Characterized by vulgar or pretentious display; designed to impress
O.example: The ostentatious display of wealth was off-putting.
The omniscient narrator revealed all characters' thoughts.

P.definition: Having a ready insight into and understanding of things
P.example: Her perspicacious analysis solved the problem.

P.definition: Having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way
P.example: The pernicious influence of negative thinking.

P.definition: Dealing with things sensibly and realistically
P.example: She took a pragmatic approach to solving the issue.

Q.definition: Representing the most perfect or typical example
Q.example: The quintessential example of Renaissance architecture.
His quixotic quest for perfect justice.

Q.definition: Complaining in a petulant or whining manner
Q.example: The querulous tone of his response.

R.definition: Able to withstand or recover quickly from difficult conditions
R.example: The resilient community rebuilt after the disaster.
The recalcitrant student refused to participate.
The scene was redolent of his childhood.

S.definition: The occurrence and development of events by chance in a happy or beneficial way
S.example: Finding his dream job was pure serendipity.

S.definition: Kept secret, especially because it would not be approved of
S.example: She cast a surreptitious glance at her phone.

S.definition: Having or showing keen mental discernment and good judgment
S.example: The sagacious advice of the experienced mentor.

T.definition: Tending to keep a firm hold of something; persistent
T.example: Her tenacious spirit helped her overcome obstacles.

T.definition: Reserved or uncommunicative in speech; saying little
T.example: The taciturn farmer rarely spoke to strangers.

T.definition: A feeling of fear or anxiety about something that may happen
T.example: She approached the interview with trepidation.

U.example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.
The urbane host made everyone feel comfortable.

V.definition: Accorded a great deal of respect, especially because of age, wisdom, or character
V.example: The venerable old professor was highly respected.

V.definition: Using or containing more words than needed
V.example: The verbose report could have been more concise.

W.example: The garden was decorated with whimsical sculptures.

W.definition: Having or showing a feeling of vague or regretful longing
W.example: She gave a wistful smile as she remembered her childhood.

W.definition: Attractive or appealing in appearance or character
W.example: Her winsome personality charmed everyone she met.

X.definition: Relating to hospitality between host and guest
X.example: The xenial atmosphere made everyone feel welcome.

X.definition: Yellow; having yellow or fair hair
X.example: The xanthous flowers brightened the garden.

X.definition: Characterized by dryness, especially of the skin
X.example: The xerotic climate affected their skin.

Y.definition: A strong feeling of desire or longing
Y.example: She felt a yearning for her childhood home.

Y.definition: Tending to give way under pressure; compliant
Y.example: The yielding nature of the soft soil.

Y.definition: Having characteristics of young people; vigorous and fresh
Y.example: He maintained a youthful outlook on life.

Z.definition: Having or showing zeal; ardent, enthusiastic
Z.example: The zealous student spent extra hours studying.
The zephyr brought relief on the hot summer day.

Z.definition: The highest point reached by a celestial or other object
Z.example: The company had reached the zenith of its success.
